summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 25%), left ventricular thrombus, chronic kidney disease, diabetes, and prior AAA repair was admitted for evaluation of bright red blood per rectum. He had a therapeutic INR of 4.0 prior to admission, and labs showed a drop in hematocrit from baseline (41.5% to 31.6%) over 24 hours, though he remained hemodynamically stable. CT abdomen showed a mild caliber change at the splenic flexure, but no acute pathology. Colonoscopy and EGD revealed no active bleeding source, though blood was present in the cecum. Capsule endoscopy identified a slow bleed from a mucosal lesion in the distal jejunum. Given the stability of his hemoglobin and the high risk of thromboembolism from his known LV thrombus, anticoagulation was resumed with warfarin, bridged by heparin. His beta-blocker and diuretic were temporarily held but restarted as his condition stabilized. He was discharged home on warfarin, with a bowel regimen, and scheduled for outpatient double balloon enteroscopy to treat the bleeding site.
